newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to improve human rights.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to improve human rights.

text.p: Turkey is planning to implement a series of measures aimed at improving its human rights record, a long-term target of criticism from its European partners, the foreign ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

It said the proposals, announced after a meeting between police, foreign and interior ministry officials, focused on preventing torture in police custody, strengthening efforts to find missing people and increasing freedom of expression.
"Our goal is to drop the issue of human rights both from the agenda of Turkey and from the Turkish-EU relationship before the end of this year," the statement said.

The European Parliament has blocked millions of dollars of aid to Turkey, partly as a result of its human rights record. Last week, senior European politicians spoke out against Turkey's membership of the European Union.
The foreign ministry statement said regional governors and police chiefs had been instructed to monitor human rights practices and prevent prisoners being ill-treated.
"We cannot tolerate ill-treatment of our citizens and harm the prestige of our state to hide the wrongdoing of a police officer," it said.
The office of Turkish President Suleyman Demirel announced on Tuesday he had approved a law passed by parliament last week which reformed custody procedures in Turkey.
The new law most notably reduces the maximum detention period for collective crimes in Turkey's nine emergency rule provinces to one week from 30 days previously.

The foreign ministry statement said there were also plans to end the imprisonment of writers and journalists on crimes of conscience and "upgrade the freedom of expression to the level of Western Europe".

The activities of the recently established Missing Persons Bureau would be strengthened and an undersecretary committee will be established to monitor the implementation of these measures, the statement added.
